title: SDK tutorial fixes & sample app TODO (personal scratchpad)
content:
Quick context:
- Started triaging onboarding tutorials after feedback from outreach last week. Focus is on: 1) short quickstart that actually runs in ~5 minutes; 2) a sample chat app that demonstrates streaming and function calling; 3) a tiny embed+search demo for the guide.

Open tickets / priorities (rough):
- High: Quickstart README + tiny config file (ENGDOC-348). Many users drop off on the docker-compose step. Put a single-file docker run example first.
- High: Fix sample-chat for streaming (GH #672) — current example uses blocking read; breaks with node streaming SDK.
- Med: Add test harness for the sample-embed pipeline so we don't ship regressions.
- Low: Add language selector for tutorials (en/es) — can defer but leave placeholders.

Immediate fixes to do (today / pairing slot):
1) Replace docker-compose example with single-run command (Docker Desktop path) + note about env vars.
   - Action: write command, test on Mac + Linux.
   - Quick snippet: docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=... redwood/sdk-quickstart:latest sh -c 'python quickstart.py'
2) Streaming demo: patch example to use SDK.stream(). Add comment about chunk boundaries and partial JSON.
   - Edge case: if user passes model override with short context, SDK currently throws TypeError in parse. Add guard and test.
3) Tutorial code: put copy/paste-ready snippets at top of the page (no imports hidden).

Sample app checklist (sample-chat):
- [ ] README: one-liner + run steps + expected output screenshot (GIF).
- [ ] Fix handler for function-calls example so it returns structured JSON and not plain text.
- [ ] Add minimal unit test that runs the chat script with a mocked response (CI cheap smoke test).
- [ ] Add note about latency expectations on Hosted vs Dedicated (link to console metrics).

Search/embedding mini-demo thoughts:
- Keep dataset tiny (3 docs) so it runs instantly in CI. Show code for: create-embedding -> upsert -> simple cosine search -> rerank.
- Show quantized-embed model caveat (doc-level note): results may differ slightly, add quality check snippet.

Unresolved questions / decisions to make:
- Do we standardize a single logging snippet across tutorials? (pro: consistent debugging; con: might leak patterns users shouldn't copy)
- How opinionated should quickstart be about auth? Right now examples use REDWOOD_API_KEY env; want to include local key-file option?
- Do we keep the language selector live or generate translations in a separate repo?

Notes to self (short):
- When writing README keep lines < 80 chars for better rendered diffs.
- Use GH Action to lint code blocks in MD (there's an existing action in infra repo).
- Coordinate with Solutions Eng to record a 6-min walkthrough video for sample-chat.

Pairing plan (Thu 10–11am):
- Goal: land the streaming fix + update quickstart. Ravi joins for streaming debug. Lina reviews README wording.
- Bring a reproducible failing case: a small node script that reproduces the blocking read in < 10s.

Minimal PR checklist (for me):
- [ ] Local test passes (python or node smoke).
- [ ] Markdown renders in GH preview with codeblocks highlighted.
- [ ] Update CHANGELOG under docs/quickstart.
- [ ] Add linked tickets to PR description.

One-liners / voice notes to paste into PRs: "Switch quickstart to a single docker run to reduce friction; preserves docker-compose as optional. Streaming demo now uses SDK.stream with buffering guard to avoid partial-JSON parse errors."

Risks / notes for follow-up:
- Streaming changes might require a minor SDK bump; coordinate release notes.
- Embedding quality tests should run weekly to avoid silent regressions when model catalog updates.

Next steps (by EOD Friday):
- Draft PR for quickstart and sample-chat streaming fix.
- Create tiny CI smoke test for sample-chat that runs in matrix (node/python).
- Ping Solutions Eng to schedule 15-min recording.

Random TODOs (scratch):
- capture GIF for expected streaming behavior
- check if stable diffusion image in sample app needs license note
- re-run tutorial on Windows machine (VM) to catch path issues

-- end of scratchpad --

(If this doc sits idle for > 7 days, prune into a Confluence follow-up and close low-priority todos.)
